summary.value: This paper proposes HiSo, a novel Hessian-informed zeroth-order optimization method for federated learning that achieves dimension-free communication while accelerating convergence. The key innovation lies in leveraging global diagonal Hessian approximations as preconditioners without transmitting second-order information, thus preserving the scalar-only communication paradigm. Theoretically, the authors establish a convergence rate independent of model dimension and Lipschitz constant under certain Hessian approximation assumptions, providing the first such result for ZO methods in FL with multiple local updates. Empirically, HiSo demonstrates 1-5× speedup in communication rounds and up to 90 million times communication savings compared to first-order baselines across diverse LLM fine-tuning tasks.
